draft.title: Persian and Peloponnesian Wars
card: In the early 400s BCE, the Persian Empire invaded Greece. Many Greek city-states joined forces to fight it, even though they were often rivals.
The Athenians won at Marathon in 490 BCE. At the sea battle of Salamis in 480 BCE, the Greek fleet defeated the Persian navy. The Greeks won the war.
After Persia was beaten, Athens and Sparta became rivals. Each led a group of allied city-states, and they fought each other for many years from 431 BCE.
Sparta won the Peloponnesian War in 404 BCE. Athens was weakened by the long fighting, and the Greeks went from fighting a common enemy to fighting each other.
draft.remember: Greeks united against Persia and won. Then Athens and Sparta fought each other, and Sparta won.

a.q: Which statement best describes how the two wars were different?
opts: Greeks fought Persia together, then fought each other
Greeks fought each other first, then joined against Persia
Greeks fought Persia alone, with Athens against Sparta
Greeks fought at sea against Persia and on land after
a.why: In the Persian Wars many city-states joined forces against an outside enemy. In the Peloponnesian War, Athens and Sparta led groups of Greek states against each other. The second option has the order the wrong way round, because Persia came first.
a.clue: Who was the enemy in each war, and which came first?

b.q: Kallis is a Greek sailor in 480 BCE. He fights at Salamis, where the Greek fleet defeats the enemy navy. Who is the enemy?
b.why: Salamis was a sea battle in the Persian Wars, where the Greek fleet defeated the Persian navy. Sparta and Athens were Greek, and they fought each other later, in the Peloponnesian War.
b.clue: Salamis was part of the earlier war.

wants.brief: A map of Greece and the Aegean Sea showing Athens, Sparta, Marathon and the island of Salamis, with the direction of the Persian invasion marked.
wants.why: It helps students see where the battles took place and how Persia came to Greece.

a.best: Greeks fought Persia together, then fought each other
